title: Silverwind QBR — Runway, Capacity & Roadmap Alignment
topics: dedicated vs hosted vs private deployment tradeoffs

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-09-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Lena Ortiz (Silverwind Head of ML), Marcus Chen (Silverwind Platform), Ava Gomez (Silverwind CISO), Diego Ramos (Silverwind VP Product)
Deck: https://redwood.app/decks/silverwind-qbr-sept2027 (shared)

Summary section (auto): Quick recap at top - runway concerns for upcoming product launch, cost spikes in July, interest in private/VPC with dedicated capacity, SOC2 + KMS questions.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we can start. Uh, appreciate you taking the time, this is Jordan, AE on the account. Samir's here for CSM, Priya's gonna run the technical bits.
[00:14] Lena Ortiz: Hi all, thanks, um, quick note we have a hard launch in mid-November so main thing is runway and predictability, want to make sure the platform can handle our spike.
[00:28] Jordan Lee: Great, that's the framing. Marcus, do you want to walk through current traffic and where you saw the cost spike?
[00:34] Marcus Chen: Yeah sure, so in July we had a 3x burst during the marketing window, p95 latency crept from 180ms to about 520ms on the hosted plan, and token costs grew like 70% because of replays and lack of effective prefix caching. There's a couple of things - our traffic shape has high fanout, lots of short requests, and we didn't have batching tuned.
[00:58] Priya Raman: Right, and to add, on the model side you were on rwd-13b-compat quantized, which is cost efficient but has some throughput limitations under short lived heavy fanout, it helps if we tune the autoscale and batching thresholds. Also prefix/K-V cache - sorry, K-V cache - can reduce cost.
[01:21] Lena Ortiz: K-V cash?
[01:23] Priya Raman: K-V cash, yeah, the key-value cache for prefixes, sometimes comes out in the transcript as K-V cash, but it's the KV cache. It lets us avoid recomputing tokens for repeated prompts.
[01:34] Diego Ramos: Quick Q - dedicated capacity would prevent noisy neighbors, right? It would give us more predictable p95?
[01:39] Jordan Lee: Yes, Dedicated isolates GPU pools, predictable throughput. For strict p95 SLOs, customers often pick a small reserved pool plus burst capacity. We can show a model of cost vs p95.
[01:50] Ava Gomez: From security side, we care about audit logs, KMS, and SSO. Do you have SOC2 artifacts? Also how does KMS-integrate with Private? We want keys on our side.
[02:04] Samir Patel: Absolutely, we have a security pack. We support customer-managed KMS in Private and Dedicated for certain patterns; for VPC we can integrate via our KMS bridge for on-prem HSM. We'll send the SOC2 and a more detailed note on KMS/H-S-M options.
[02:21] Marcus Chen: Great — also, someone asked in our infra review about model quantization profiles, what you recommend for our workload - heavy short responses.
[02:29] Priya Raman: For short-response, lower precision quantization like 4-bit with optimized kernels usually helps throughput and cost, but quality/regression testing is important. We have a recommendation matrix: latency-sensitive -> 4-bit optimized, throughput-y -> 8-bit packing, fallback to xformer-compat models if rollout issues. We'll share the matrix.
[02:50] Lena Ortiz: Can we do a two-week benchmark? We want to mirror production traffic, see p95 and cost per 1k tokens.
[02:56] Jordan Lee: Yep, that's the plan we discussed. Priya will own the benchmark plan and Marcus will provide traces.
[03:04] Priya Raman: I'll outline the steps: 1) ingest a 48-hour traffic trace, 2) run two 7-day windows on both Hosted and Dedicated (or Private) configs, 3) capture p50/p95/p99, token cost, and autoscale behavior. We'll also test prefix caching.
[03:20] Diego Ramos: Will the Private deployment require us to change our integration? We use the Redwood API today.
[03:25] Priya Raman: No major API changes. Private gives a customer-controlled control plane and networking, same API surface. There are some config flags for routing and KMS that you will set.
[03:34] Ava Gomez: Data residency — we have EU customers, need logs to remain in EU. Can Private be deployed in our EU region?
[03:41] Samir Patel: Yes, Private in EU region is supported. We'll note the region in the compliance pack.
[03:47] [03:47] Jordan Lee: Quick pause — anyone have immediate blockers to proceeding to pilot?
[03:52] Lena Ortiz: Budget approval still open but if you can share a clear cost model and pilot pricing we can push it through.
[03:58] Jordan Lee: We'll send a pilot SKU and an example cost carve-out.
[04:02] [04:02] Marcus Chen: On the technical nit - when you say autoscale we saw cold starts and a warmup penalty in July. Is there an option for pre-warmed capacity?
[04:12] Priya Raman: Yes, Dedicated supports pre-warm instances; there's a warmup buffer. Also continuous batching can be tuned so short requests are coalesced without added latency. We'll demonstrate in the bench.
[04:25] Lena Ortiz: Also curious about rollouts — we run model experiments weekly. Can we pin model versions and do canary rollouts?
[04:33] Jordan Lee: Yep, rollouts and pinning are supported. You can define canary weights and automatic rollback on quality regression tied to your evals. We also support function/tool-calling, so you can route to new versions with A/B.
[04:46] [04:46] Diego Ramos: One more product note — our product team wants to understand which optimizations yield the biggest bang-for-buck: caching vs quantization vs batching.
[04:55] Priya Raman: We'll prepare a prioritized recommendation: 1) prefix/KV caching (quick wins), 2) batching/autoscale thresholds, 3) quantization profile and kernel selection for long-term savings. We'll attach a sample cost-savings spreadsheet.
[05:10] [05:10] Ava Gomez: For SSO, we use Okta. Any gotchas?
[05:14] Samir Patel: Okta is standard. SAML/SCIM provisioning supported. We'll include the integration guide with attribute mapping.
[05:22] [05:22] Lena Ortiz: Can you lay out timeline? If we want pilot in October, what are the steps?
[05:27] Jordan Lee: Tentative timeline: this week share pricing & security pack; week of 9/27 run planning + traffic ingest; pilot kickoff first week of October; two-week benchmark mid-October; review and go/no-go end of October.
[05:40] Marcus Chen: Sounds good. Also can you confirm whether logs include token-level breakdowns for chargeback?
[05:47] Priya Raman: Yes, console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and per token. We can share a sample export.
[05:55] [05:55] Diego Ramos: Any concerns about vendor lock? We're evaluating CloudAI and ModelServeX too.
[06:01] Jordan Lee: Fair call. Our positioning is unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private so you can move to private later without changing APIs. We'll provide an ROI comparison and migration notes.
[06:12] [06:12] Marcus Chen: One small thing - we saw an occassional misattribution in logs where multiple request IDs mapped to same session. Not sure if that was our tracing.
[06:20] Priya Raman: We'll open an ops ticket and pair with your infra to correlate traces.
[06:25] [06:25] Lena Ortiz: Okay quick recap — we want cost model, SOC2 + KMS note, benchmark plan, traffic trace. Pilot tentatively early Oct.
[06:34] Jordan Lee: Correct. I'll send pilot pricing and a sample cost spreadsheet. Priya will send the bench plan. Samir will send security docs.
[06:41] [06:41] Ava Gomez: And I'll send our compliance nuance list by Friday.
[06:45] Diego Ramos: One last question on SLAs - what uptime and p95 targets do you typically commit to on Dedicated?
[06:52] Samir Patel: For Dedicated we typically target 99.9% with a contractual p95 latency target based on model family; we'll propose a target for rwd-13b-compat and a remediation plan in the pilot.
[07:05] [07:05] Jordan Lee: Great, if no more questions let's wrap. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[07:11] Lena Ortiz: Thanks all.
[07:13] Marcus Chen: Thanks.
[07:14] [End of transcript]

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (K-V cash, H-S-M) and speaker overlaps. Action items captured separately above.
file_notes: Pilot must include EU region deployment option; customer requested token-level export and an ops pairing for trace correlation.
